title: Shadow of Rome
subtitle: Two routes through a Roman conspiracy

body: Shadow of Rome is Capcom's PlayStation 2 action-adventure, first released in Europe on 4 February 2005. A fictional account of Julius Caesar's assassination follows Agrippa, whose father is accused of the murder, and Octavianus, who investigates the charge. Their activities divide the game between gladiatorial combat and stealth. One character must survive in front of a crowd while the other searches for information without drawing attention. The contrast gives the same conspiracy two practical forms: a public struggle for survival and a quieter effort to uncover what happened.

Agrippa's sections place weapons, enemies and the audience within a single violent performance. The player has to survive the immediate fight while making use of the equipment and opportunities around the arena. Combat becomes an exaggerated spectacle, with the crowd responding to what happens in front of it. Octavianus changes the pace through infiltration and investigation, where avoiding discovery takes priority over direct force. Alternating between the two characters gives the campaign its structure, making progress in the larger mystery depend on very different kinds of action.

Motohide Eshiro directed the game, with Keiji Inafune and Yoshinori Ono producing and Yoshino Aoki and Kota Suzuki composing its music. Reviews generally welcomed the gladiatorial combat and presentation, while the slower stealth sections attracted more criticism. Capcom had begun work towards a sequel, but disappointing sales changed the plan. That follow-up developed into Dead Rising instead. Shadow of Rome therefore stands as an unusual single release, joining historical conspiracy to theatrical violence at a moment when Capcom was exploring new projects for a wider international audience.
